roles.heroLead: An Arlington bathroom gets redone about once a generation, so it had better be done right. The part that decides that isn't the tile — it's the bonded membrane behind it. We build the whole assembly, run a 24-hour flood test, photograph it passing, and only then set tile. No shortcuts, because you're not doing this twice.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Arlington, WA?
roles.costP1: Budget $14–$26 for every installed square foot of Arlington tile work. Inside that figure sit labor, substrate prep, setting materials and the tile itself; bare labor opens at $11/sq ft. A tub-shower surround generally bills out at $3,200–$6,800, with the whole bathroom — shower, niche and floor — tending to close out in the $6,500–$14,000 band.
roles.costP2: What catches most people off guard is that a tile's shape sets your labor bill, not the sticker on the carton. Tiny mosaic brings hundreds of cuts and grout joints; one oversized porcelain plank brings a handful. The layout writes the invoice.
roles.costNote: Figures reflect Arlington as of August 2026 and include tile, materials and labor. Trust the written price from your free estimate over anything on this page.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers go under and behind good tile. Every failed shower we open up in north Snohomish County is missing one of them — nine times out of ten the membrane, skipped to keep a few hundred dollars in the budget of a job that later costs five figures to tear apart.
roles.whyP1: A leaking shower never makes a sound. Moisture sneaks through grout, soaks into the substrate, then shows itself years on — a hallway floor gone spongy, a brown halo on the ceiling below the bathroom. The repair by then means subfloor and framing, fresh drywall, and tiling from the start.
roles.whyP2: Of every ten dollars a shower costs, about one goes to waterproofing. Cutting that dollar is the dearest saving a remodel can make.
roles.scopeIntro: Treat these as opening figures; layout, tile format and substrate condition all bend them. At your house we write the actual number down, free.
roles.cardShower: Pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, flood test; after that the niche, the curb or curbless entry, and tile. You're paying mostly for what disappears behind the wall — as it should be.
roles.cardFloors: Mudrooms, kitchens, entryways, baths and basements. Before any tile, the subfloor gets trued flat; where the slab shifts or a warming mat lives, an uncoupling membrane goes down.
roles.cardBacksplash: Herringbone, slab-look porcelain, subway or mosaic sheet. Outlets get tight, clean cuts, edges get proper trim, and the grout color answers to your countertop, not the box the tile came in.
roles.cardHeated: An electric mat laid over uncoupling membrane, resistance verified twice — before tiling, once after — and fed by a circuit of its own. Worth doing only when the floor is opened anyway.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked tiles, crumbling grout, corners letting go in the shower. We'll say plainly whether it's fixable or whether the substrate underneath is already gone.
roles.cardDemo: Tile, thinset and backer stripped out, dust held back with plastic and negative air, all of it hauled away. Your driveway stays clear.
roles.materialsLead: Iron-stained fixtures show what Arlington well water does to the wrong finish. The usual mistake isn't cheap tile — it's a good tile pressed into the wrong room's service. Below, the advice we'd give beside your tub, condensed.
roles.materialsNote: These rates cover the tile alone; installation is quoted separately. Samples ride along on the estimate, with honest notes on where spending more pays off.
roles.estIntro: Rough-cut versions of the sums we'd do at your kitchen table: prep, format, footage, scope. No quote comes out of it, just a number sturdy enough to plan against.
roles.daysLead: Plan an Arlington bathroom at four to six working days. The stretch that feels slowest is the waterproofing — and it's the stretch that matters most.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Arlington, WA?
roles.faqA1: Arlington tile jobs price out near $14 to $26 per square foot once installed — the tile, prep work on the substrate, setting materials and labor all ride inside that spread, and labor alone begins at $11 for each square foot. Figure $3,200 up to $6,800 for a typical tub-shower surround; a bathroom done complete — floor, shower, niche — settles around $6,500 to $14,000. Format, more than sticker price, is what moves cost: mosaic sheets and large-format alike ask considerably more labor per foot than plain 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Arlington?
roles.faqA2: Tiling out a standard alcove shower in Arlington means $3,200–$6,800 — a figure which folds in demolition, the bonded waterproofing build, a pre-sloped pan, setting the tile, a niche and the grout. Push past standard — benches, curbless entries, full-height stone, steam — and the price follows. Waterproofing amounts to maybe a tenth of the bill, yet it's the piece that spares you a failure running into the tens of thousands.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Without exception. Every shower we build carries a bonded waterproofing system behind its tile — never cement board alone with thinset on top. The base comes pre-sloped; a liquid or sheet membrane climbs the walls; corners, seams and pipe penetrations all get sealed; and photos document a 24-hour flood test before we set anything. Water rolls off grout and tile, but nothing about them is waterproof — the membrane is what stands between water and your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Start to finish, an Arlington bathroom needs four to six working days: dust containment and demo first; substrate and waterproofing next, with 24 hours of flood-test water standing on the new membrane; setting takes a day, maybe two; then comes the close-out of grout, silicone and trim. Give the finished shower 24 hours to cure before using it. A floor alone typically wraps inside one or two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain, wherever water or foot traffic is involved. Denser than ceramic, it absorbs below 0.5% water, shrugs off chips, and its glaze resists the iron tint hard Arlington well water leaves behind on softer surfaces. Ceramic belongs on backsplashes and walls, where duty is light and the savings are real. The rule we work by: floors and shower floors get porcelain; the merely decorative spots can take ceramic or glass.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: We do — often. Under-tile electric radiant adds somewhere near $11–$16 per square foot installed, thermostat in the price. The mat sits atop an uncoupling membrane, resistance measured before the tile goes down and again after, power from a dedicated circuit. The economics work exactly once: while the floor is open. Retrofitting means demolishing finished tile.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Almost every time, yes. Tear-out with haul-away prices around $3.50 per square foot, and what it buys is sight of the subfloor — evidence of rot, of movement, of how finished height will land at each doorway. Setting new tile over old can succeed when the existing surface is flat, solid and firmly bonded, but it raises the floor and entombs whatever is wrong below it. Problems found at demo cost less than problems found after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Arlington?
roles.faqA8: In Arlington, a standard 30 square foot backsplash installs for $1,100 up to $2,200 — outlet openings cut, edges trimmed, grout keyed to the countertop. Reaching the upper end takes a labor-hungry layout: herringbone, mosaic sheeting, a framed feature behind the range, or slab-look porcelain that climbs clear to the ceiling. Plain subway keeps you near the bottom figure.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently, yes. Pricing for repair and regrout opens at $8 per square foot — right for grout that's stained or breaking apart, a tile or two cracked by a dropped pan, or shower corners where tired grout needs cutting out for silicone. When tiles sound hollow underfoot, release in a spreading pattern, or a wall yields to pressure, the substrate itself has failed, and patching it merely borrows time. Before quoting, we tell you which situation you're in.
roles.faqQ10: Which Arlington neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Arlington — Downtown and the blocks off Olympic Avenue, Gleneagle, Smokey Point, Kent Prairie, Arlington Heights, Sisco Heights, Trafton, Cicero and Bryant — plus the surrounding country toward Silvana, Island Crossing, Lakewood and Oso. We also tile in Marysville, Stanwood, Granite Falls, Lake Stevens and across north Snohomish County.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: A 2-year workmanship warranty rides on every OC Flooring tile install — twice the coverage carpet gets, because tile trouble tends to surface in year two, not in week two. Install a waterproofing maker's full assembly and their system coverage stacks over ours. The membrane and the flood test both get photographed, which means proof of what's behind your wall exists whenever you sell.
roles.hoodsOut: Don't see your area? If Arlington sits within about an hour's drive of you, we'll come — mention your location when booking.
